mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority / licensed notary in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) for each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider / financial institution in country of origin, attested by a licensed notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional reference letter from a licensed bank or legal practitioner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or law firm in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association signed by subscriber (where incorporated elsewhere)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, and UBOs against local designated persons lists, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, and Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit regulations; enhanced due diligence required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates; risk-based customer due diligence must be documented before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry (SICR) administered by the Office of the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in English or Samoan using the Latin alphabet; Chinese characters and non-Latin scripts are not accepted and must be transliterated into Latin characters; the name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered company or reserved name and must include a permissible suffix such as 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Inc' or 'Ltd'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of a rejection notice, the applicant or licensed registered agent may file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, stating the grounds for review; if the Registrar affirms the rejection, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 28 days; final recourse is available by judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible for domestic administrative purposes, but a registered office and registered agent in Samoa are mandatory; for this industry, no physical staff or dedicated local premises are required by statute, although the OECD pillar-two and Samoan economic substance guidelines encourage demonstrable local decision-making and activity for entities operating in active business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated less than 5% annual probability for a standard low-risk International Company in the consultancy sector; risk increases if economic substance filings indicate no local operations or if AML/CFT suspicion is raised.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 2015 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies Amendment Act 2016, Part 2 (Incorporation), ss. 6–12, and Part 4 (Registered Office, Directors and Officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) — Registrar of International Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Association filed via a SIFA-licensed International Service Provider
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required; share capital may be denominated in any currency acceptable under the Act and no escrow account obligation applies for standard consulting structures
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company's Articles of Association, as filed with the Registrar of International Companies under the International Companies Act 2015, be adopted in their entirety, and that the share subscription made by the subscriber be duly accepted and recorded as fully paid in the register of members. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be established at the office of its licensed service provider in Apia, Samoa. RESOLVED, that [Director Name] and [Second Director Name] be appointed as the first directors, and that [Secretary Name] be appointed as Corporate Secretary, each to hold office until otherwise determined in accordance with the Articles. RESOLVED, that the appointed officers be authorised to open bank accounts, appoint corresponding agents, and execute all ancillary agreements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) — Registration and Licensing Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a SIFA-licensed International Service Provider to submit a name reservation application via the SIFA digital portal. The proposed corporate name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered entity and must include a permissible suffix such as 'Limited'. Await written clearance of the reserved name.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation charter draft or name clause
Engagement letter with licensed service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an alternative name reservation within 5 business days; no fee is forfeited and revisions may be submitted through the same licensed service provider.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA — Registrar of International Companies (through licensed agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed service provider drafts the Articles of Association including share classes, director powers, indemnity provisions, and tax-exempt election language. The subscriber(s) execute the Articles and supporting consents, and the provider completes statutory declaration of compliance.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (each director)
Subscriber details and share allocation schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns a requisition, amend the Articles within 10 business days through the licensed provider, cure the noted defect, and resubmit without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Ministry of Finance — Treasury (collection via SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Remit the official government incorporation fee of USD 100, plus the licensed agent's professional fee, by bank wire or SIFA-approved electronic payment. Retain the payment receipt as evidence of settlement of statutory duties.
required_dossiers: Bank wire confirmation or payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is misapplied, present the wire confirmation to SIFA treasury for reconciliation; re-issuance of the official receipt is obtained within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance of the Articles and confirmation of fee payment, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under seal, evidencing the legal existence of the International Company with limited liability and tax-exempt status within Samoa's international zone.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance is delayed beyond the SLA, the licensed provider files a formal follow-up with the Registrar; any administrative objection is curable by submitting a revised declaration or corrected particulars within 7 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Corporate Governance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board (convened by registered agent in Apia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The first directors convene an initial meeting (or pass unanimous written resolutions) to adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution: subscribe shares, adopt the Articles, fix the registered office, appoint directors/officers, and authorise bank account opening. Minutes are recorded in the register of minutes.
required_dossiers: Share certificates and register of members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum is not achieved, adjourn the meeting and obtain unanimous written resolutions in lieu of a meeting; recusal rules are applied in accordance with the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office, Agent Confirmation and Post-Incorporation Compliance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA — Registrar of International Companies (via licensed agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File confirmation of the registered office address in Samoa and the appointment of the licensed International Service Provider as registered agent. Undertake annual exemption maintenance filings, maintain statutory registers at the registered office, and open the operational bank account using the incorporation package.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and appointment form
Certificate of Incorporation and Articles (certified copies)
Bank account opening package (Wise Business or bank wire instructions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return or registered agent filing is rejected, correct the particulars and refile within 14 days; late-filing penalties are waived upon demonstrated good faith correction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) — Licensing and Compliance Division (own the International Company charter; no separate industrial board applies to consultancy activities)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Company Certificate of Incorporation (serves as the operating charter for cross-border market entry consultancy; no additional sectoral operating permit required under ISIC 7020)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) — Environmental Assessment and Monitoring Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category D — office-based consultancy-only activity with no physical installation, manufacturing, or land disturbance; no EIA Report or Registration required)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero industrial discharge; office operations must observe general municipal wastewater and solid waste disposal rules under the Water Resources Management Act 2008 and the Waste Management Act 2011

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a pure advisory office presence; where a physical office is leased in Apia, the premises must hold a fire safety clearance from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) and comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2006 for workplace safety; no structural load inspection or manufacturing clearance applies.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Ministry for Revenue – Online Services portal (www.sra.gov.ws)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Samoa International Company (IC) does not automatically obtain a general income TIN because the IC is statutorily tax-exempt under the International Companies Act 2012. The IC must be registered with the Samoa Registrar of Companies, obtaining a Registry/IC number and annual government fee receipt. If the IC nevertheless undertakes a taxable activity requiring VAGST registration, it must submit Form VAGST-REG to SRA, provide constitutional documents, director and shareholder identification, proof of the registered office in Samoa, and bank account details; SRA then issues a VAGST registration number and tax compliance certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under Samoa law. The International Company is automatically treated as a tax-exempt offshore entity; no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election is available under Samoa domestic tax legislation. For U.S. federal tax purposes, the entity may independently file IRS Form 8832 to elect classification, but this does not alter Samoa tax exemption.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or national e-invoicing API/digital stamping regime exists in Samoa. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue standard tax invoices containing the supplier's SRA VAGST registration number, and retain all source records for at least 7 years for audit and SRA accessibility.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies to: (1) goods physically exported from Samoa within the prescribed time, (2) services supplied directly to a non-resident person who is outside Samoa at the time supply occurs, (3) international transport or ancillary services, and (4) supplies to a non-resident in a duty-free or offshore zone. The claimant must be a VAGST-registered person and must hold contemporaneous documentation proving export, overseas receipt, and the non-resident status of the customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SRA Customs Form CED)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign exchange record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claims are subject to SRA audit, reassessment, full clawback of the claimed VAT credit, and imposition of late payment penalties and statutory interest. Civil penalties may reach up to 100% of the tax shortfall, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud carries substantial fines and imprisonment under the VAGST Act 2005 and the Tax Administration Act 2012. SRA may also cancel VAGST registration of repeat offenders.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), acting as the exchange-control authority under the Exchange Control Act 1970 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1971, administered through licensed authorized dealers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa operates a partially convertible, managed-float currency (Samoan Tala, WST). Current-account transactions are freely convertible for documented commercial flows through licensed authorized dealers; capital-account transactions require Central Bank approval unless a statutory exemption applies. A Samoa International Company (IC) is treated as a non-resident enterprise for exchange-control purposes: foreign-currency receipts may be freely credited, held and remitted offshore without CBS approval in USD, AUD, NZD or EUR, and profit or dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted when paid out of wholly foreign-currency reserves. The residual convertibility hurdles are (i) conversion of external earnings into WST and (ii) any payment to a Samoan resident, each requiring documentary substantiation and CBS balance-of-payments reporting through the authorized dealer. The IC is statutorily barred from conducting any domestic Samoan business, thereby insulating its treasury flows from the domestic convertibility regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods-export statutory baseline under the Exchange Control Regulations 1971: payment for exports must be received within 180 days of shipment; the exporter must offer the foreign-currency proceeds to an authorized dealer within one month of receipt; and the default surrender or conversion ratio is 100% unless the CBS has granted a general or specific working-balance retention exemption. For the WS_IC market-entry consultancy model, service-export receivables are 'invisible' foreign-currency receipts payable by non-residents; because the IC holds a designated foreign-currency account, performs no domestic trade, and is outside the Samoan resident economy, the proceeds are exempt from compulsory surrender and may be retained indefinitely in USD, netted against offshore operating costs, or voluntarily converted to WST. Any WST conversion nevertheless creates a controlled balance that cannot be disbursed to a Samoan resident without an underlying service contract and an authorized-dealer CBS declaration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific Limited - Samoa Branch (BSP Samoa)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account - USD/AUD/NZD multi-currency account with WST settlement sub-account
Capital Escrow Account - USD-denominated escrow for inbound share subscription and capital-injection verification

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High. Wise B2B and similarly regulated offshore EMIs will ordinarily onboard a Samoa-registered International Company when the UBO structure is transparent and the company demonstrates genuine non-resident activity through executed market-entry consultancy contracts. Legal constraints: (i) Samoa imposes no licensing requirement or prohibition on an IC maintaining a settlement account at an offshore EMI, but the EMI must not hold itself out as a Samoan authorized dealer, must not execute WST-denominated payments, and must respond to lawful Samoan FIU information requests; (ii) the EMI balance is an 'external asset' that remains permissible under the Exchange Control Act only where no Samoan-resident transaction is settled through it; (iii) EMIs routinely reject a bare registered-agent address in Apia as insufficient substantive proof of place of business, so the IC should maintain a verifiable serviced-office lease or sublease, a physical operating address in the target market, and a bank reference from the CBS-licensed account. Recommended structure: Wise B2B as the daily collection and disbursement rail for sub-USD 100,000 consultancy fees, with the BSP Samoa or SCB account as the formal clearing, capital and escalation account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement mandates physical appearance. The Samoa KYC Guidelines issued by the Financial Intelligence Unit empower each licensed bank to set its own onboarding standard. BSP Samoa accepts fully remote onboarding of non-resident directors using live video verification, digital passport capture and electronic corporate-document review. SCB requires either one director to attend an interview at an Apia branch or notarized and apostilled certified copies of all signatory passports together with a video interview conducted by the bank's compliance officer. NBS in practice requires physical branch presence for the initial mandate unless a licensed International Company agent or referral professional sponsors the account. Recommended compliance posture: the IC appoints a Samoan-resident licensed International Company agent or arranges for one director to appear in branch for the initial signing; all subsequent signings and treasury operations proceed remotely under the bank's electronic banking mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Samoan authorized dealer flags the IC as a 'shell company' because of the zero minimum paid-up capital, statutory tax-exempt status and absence of local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and certificate of good standing under the International Companies Act 1987; statutory declaration of the IC; licensed registered-agent services agreement evidencing the Apia registered office; current share register and ultimate beneficial ownership schedule; tax-exemption certificate issued by the Samoa Ministry of Revenue; board resolution defining the overseas market-entry consultancy mandate; 24-month management projections; and audited or exemption-qualified financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or UBOs from jurisdictions on the FATF or regional watch list trigger enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Police clearance certificate or financial-conduct reference from each director's home regulator; Samoan FIU anti-money-laundering and counter-financing-of-terrorism self-declaration; notarized passport and proof of residence for every 10% or greater UBO; banker's reference from a regulated home-country bank; and a source-of-wealth statement supported by 12 months of bank statements or asset ownership records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Forecasted consultancy turnover does not reconcile with actual inbound credits after the first two quarters of account activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client engagement agreements for the named target market jurisdictions; invoice register and payment schedules; signed CBS purpose-code declarations for each inward credit; a rolling 12-month cash-flow forecast tied to named clients; letters of appointment from market principals; and a written explanation of any lapsed or deferred projects.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank compliance applies 'front-company' red flags when several Samoan ICs share the same resident agent, directors and mailing address
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board minutes and a distinct delegation-of-authority policy for the WS_IC; segregated accounting ledgers; group structure diagram; intercompany transfer-pricing documentation where fees flow within a corporate group; statutory directors' and members' registers maintained solely for this IC; and the IC's dedicated AML/CFT internal controls manual, customer-due-diligence record and document-retention policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the non-resident investor wires via SWIFT MT103, or MT202 COV for an interbank-tiered credit, to the IC's USD Operational Account at BSP Samoa or the SCB Capital Escrow Account. The wire must carry ISO 20022 purpose code INVS (Investment) and tag 70 free text reading 'Share subscription - International Company - International Companies Act 1987 - external capital account'. The authorized dealer records the credit as a CBS balance-of-payments item 'Direct investment - equity injection to non-resident enterprise' and no prior CBS approval is required because the IC is exchange-control-exempt for external foreign-currency credits. The bank's verification pack comprises: (i) the parent or shareholder board resolution authorizing the investment; (ii) the IC board resolution allotting shares and confirming that no minimum capital requirement applies; (iii) an executed share subscription agreement; (iv) a UBO declaration for all 10% or greater owners; and (v) source-of-funds evidence where the credit exceeds USD 100,000. Where the bank places the capital in escrow pending source verification, release into the operational account occurs upon submission of the subscription agreement and completion of CBS reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operating disbursements, including subcontractor fees, licensing agency payments, marketing and travel, use SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers with the applicable ISO 20022 purpose code, principally FEEX for professional service fees, executed directly from the USD operating account without CBS approval. Large project settlements under a market-entry mandate that includes procurement logistics are cleared through a UCP600-compliant Commercial Letter of Credit or an ICC bank payment obligation issued via the BSP Samoa trade desk. Interbank liquidity concentration between the Wise B2B settlement pool and the CBS-licensed BSP account is effected through SWIFT MT202 COV cover payments. WST conversion for payments to Samoan residents requires the dealer to complete the CBS declaration and, where applicable, the authorized-dealer application form supported by the underlying service contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/WST forward contracts with an authorized dealer (BSP Samoa or SCB), available solely against documented current-account exposure evidenced by signed consultancy contracts, with a maximum tenor of 12 months.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/WST executed with a licensed non-resident bank; permissible for the WS_IC because settlement is effected entirely offshore with no onshore WST movement, requiring only CBS notification through the dealer's balance-of-payments reporting.
Cross-currency swaps between USD and WST with an authorized dealer, subject to prior CBS exchange-control approval and verified matching of the underlying receivables or payables.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Renewal Fee (International Company annual license fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of incorporation; payable within 30 days of the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a 10% surcharge on the unpaid fee; continued non-payment beyond one year may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution under the International Companies Act 1987.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due within 30 days of each incorporation anniversary, submitted together with the annual renewal fee.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default in filing attracts a monetary late filing penalty; persistent default exposes the company to strike-off, and directors remain personally liable for statutory penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership and Shareholding Confirmation (registered agent annual CDD/UBO review)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed registered agent (mandatory maintenance under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018); not filed with SIFA.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At minimum, on each incorporation anniversary and without undue delay upon any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain accurate BO records constitutes an AML/CFT compliance breach attributable to the registered agent; the company may face enforcement action and the agent may be subject to sanctions under the AML/CFT Act 2018.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None applicable to a standard Samoa International Company. The International Companies Act 1987 does not impose a compulsory audit for exempt international companies; an audit is required only if the memorandum or articles of incorporation mandate it or the board or members so resolve.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is the market standard; accounting records must fairly reflect the company's financial position. Audited financial statements are not filed with SIFA for a standard exempt International Company.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must confirm annually with its licensed registered agent the registered shareholders, any share transfers effected during the year, and the ultimate beneficial owners. No public UBO registry exists; the agent must hold current CDD/KYC documentation. Share transfers or beneficial ownership changes must be notified to the agent at the time of the change rather than filed with SIFA.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – 400 per annum (licensed registered agent plus Samoa registered office)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required for an exempt International Company; voluntary audited accounts approximately USD 1,500 – 3,000 if demanded by bankers or investors

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Samoa International Companies (ICs) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 are statutorily exempt from all Samoan income tax, corporate income tax, capital gains tax, dividend distribution tax, and stamp or transfer duties. The effective tax rate on foreign-sourced market entry consultancy income is therefore nil. By contrast, an ordinary non-exempt Samoa resident company is subject to the domestic headline corporate income tax rate of 27%. The IC exemption is conditional on compliance with the prohibition on carrying on business with Samoa residents, maintenance of a licensed registered agent, and annual registry filings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return (AR/IC Form) – Registrar of International Companies, administered through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Electronic Registry portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due within 30 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation. No fiscal year-end extension or tax filing deadline applies because the IC is not an income-tax filer; the Annual Return is the sole recurring statutory return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name and International Companies Registry number as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact registered name; no bilingual or translated trade names are accepted unless registered as a secondary name.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in Samoa and the name of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot act as the registered office; a Samoan licensed agent (trust or corporate service provider) must be appointed and its consent confirmed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors and shareholders register confirmation - full names, residential addresses, and shareholding details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident natural persons may use foreign residential addresses; a service address is acceptable, but SIFA may require passport copies and proof of identity on request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of no local business activity, confirming that the IC has not undertaken trade with Samoa residents, owned Samoan land, or carried on business within Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors must expressly declare that all consultancy clients are outside Samoa and that no revenue has Samoan source; an affirmative entry forfeits exempt status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Economic substance and AML compliance declaration confirming maintenance of accounting records, beneficial ownership register, and substance documentation where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident principals must identify the ultimate beneficial owner and confirm that any market-entry consultancy activity that is a relevant activity has adequate substance in Samoa.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an immediate registry penalty of WST 200 for the first default, with a daily surcharge of WST 10 for each day of continued non-compliance. Persistent non-filing for three months or more triggers suspension of the IC's good standing; after six months of default the Registrar may strike the company off the International Companies Register, causing asset vesting and legal disability. Reinstatement is conditioned on payment of all arrear fees, penalties, and a reinstatement fee.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on distributions from a Samoa International Company because the IC is tax-exempt and dividend distributions are not subject to Samoan withholding tax. For ordinary non-exempt Samoa companies, the domestic non-resident dividend withholding tax rate is 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa has a narrow double taxation agreement network; the principal applicable instrument is the Samoa - New Zealand DTA. To invoke treaty relief the non-resident recipient must (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its own domestic tax authority, (ii) submit the TRC together with a completed treaty claim form and a statement of beneficial ownership to the Samoan payer and the Samoa Ministry of Revenue before the payment due date, and (iii) procure certification from the Samoan registered agent confirming the IC's exempt status and the absence of Samoan-source income. In practice no WHT relief is required for IC distributions because the statutory rate is already zero.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates for ordinary Samoa taxpayers: royalties paid to non-residents 15%, interest paid to non-residents 10%. For an exempt International Company, outbound royalty and interest payments are subject to 0% Samoan withholding tax, and inbound foreign royalty or interest income is exempt from Samoan income tax. Under the Samoa - New Zealand DTA, general cross-border royalty and interest payments may be reduced to a maximum of 10%, subject to TRC and beneficial ownership certification.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory WST filing threshold has been established for exempt International Companies; they are not required to prepare Local File or Master File documentation because they have zero Samoan taxable income. For taxable Samoa resident companies, the Minister of Revenue retains discretionary authority to demand contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation where cross-border related-party transactions exceed commercially material levels; the arm's length principle applies under the Income Tax Act 2012.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Samoa International Finance Authority administers economic substance requirements for International Companies. A Samoa IC deriving income from relevant activities, which may include market entry consultancy, service-centre operations, headquarters functions, and intellectual property holding, must demonstrate substantial economic presence in Samoa: a physical office or premises, a minimum complement of employees, sufficient operating expenditure, and board management and decision-making conducted in Samoa. Pure consultancy invoicing without local substance is disallowed; arrangement with zero substance is rebuttably presumed to be a shell company subject to SIFA investigation, information exchange, and deregistration risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Abuse of Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the International Company to receive income from clients physically in Samoa, carrying on business with Samoan residents, owning Samoan real property, or mischaracterizing Samoan-source service revenue as offshore income to exploit the 0% IC rate; inflating deductible fees or fabricating transactions to extract funds without substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive revocation of the IC tax exemption, assessment of domestic corporate income tax at 27% on all income derived, late payment interest, and penalties of up to 200% of the tax avoided. The company may be struck off by the Registrar, and the registered agent may lose its SIFA licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are exposed to piercing of the corporate veil: civil restitution orders for the tax shortfall, asset tracing, travel bans, disqualification from holding directorship in Samoa, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud carrying imprisonment of up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an offshore invoice shell with no physical office, no staff, no bank accounts in Samoa, no board meeting minutes, and no economic substance declaration while booking consultancy fees; using the IC merely to channel fees through WISE B2B or bank wire rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalty under the International Companies Act and SIFA practice of up to WST 100,000; compulsory deregistration and dissolution; referral to the Samoa exchange of information competence for automatic exchange of information under OECD standards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for false substance declarations; they may be ordered to reimburse regulatory costs, banned from managing any Samoa company for up to 10 years, and subjected to travel restrictions pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Beneficial Ownership Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain an internal AML compliance programme, beneficial ownership register, client due diligence files, and suspicious transaction reports; processing third-party fees without verifying ultimate beneficial owners; using the IC to launder the proceeds of fraud or corruption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal liability under the Money Laundering and Prevention of Terrorism Act with fines up to WST 2,000,000 and seizure/freezing of bank accounts; SIFA suspension or revocation of the registered agent's licence; corporate dissolution for non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face direct criminal indictment, confiscation of personal assets, travel bans during prosecution, and imprisonment of up to seven years for money laundering; civil liability to third parties for loss arising from wilful blindness.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Filings and False Annual Return Declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a false Annual Return, concealing the true beneficial owner, falsely declaring no local activity, or omitting economic substance information to mislead the Registrar or SIFA while the IC in fact operates as a Samoan commercial undertaking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Statutory offence with monetary penalties per offence and a daily fine for continuing false certification; the Registry may cancel registration with immediate effect, invalidate the corporate structure, and refer the matter to the Office of the Attorney General for criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for fraudulent trading; courts may order restitution and compensation to the Registry or injured parties, impose travel bans until restitution is satisfied, and impose custodial sentences of up to five years for perjury in registry filings.
